subject: Priority escalation: checkout throughput & 500s - post-incident commitments
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@blueskyretail.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Lisa Park <lisa.park@blueskyretail.com>, accounts@blueskyretail.com
Date: 2028-05-09T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Severe degradation during peak - checkout failures and throughput drop (May 8-9)

Marissa / Redwood team,

We observed a sustained throughput degradation starting 2028-05-08 22:40 UTC and recurring spikes of 500 errors during our peak window (checkout). Our telemetry shows token-level latencies spiking from median ~120ms to >1.2s for a subset of requests and error rate climbed to ~4.8% for checkout-related routes. This has caused visible business impact (abandoned carts, payment errors).

We need:
- An immediate exec readout and a concrete remediation plan with owners and dates.
- Confirmation this will not reoccur in our coming flash sale next week.
- Artifacts: timeline, root cause, and mitigations.

Please escalate — we are looping in our Director of Ops (Lisa) and billing team.

Jordan
Director of Engineering
BlueSky Retail

P.S. attaching the top-level error sample we pulled from our side (we'll send logs if helpful).
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@blueskyretail.com>
Cc: Lisa Park <lisa.park@blueskyretail.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-09T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Severe degradation during peak - checkout failures and throughput drop (May 8-9)

Jordan — thanks for the heads up and very sorry for the impact. We’ve prioritized this and I’ll lead the exec readout. Proposed immediate steps:

1) 30-min readout today at 11:00 PT — attendees: Kara (Customer Success), Karthik (Infra), Grace (Ops lead), Ben (Sales lead) + your ops/eng leads.
2) Triage runbook execution and temporary routing to our dedicated small-pool fallback for checkout routes (if accepted) to stabilize.
3) Deliverables by EOD today: draft timeline and RCA, action owners + 7-day remediation commitments.

I’ve attached a brief acknowledgement note we share with customers during incidents (initial-acknowledgement.txt). I’ll send calendar invite in 5 mins.

—Marissa
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jordan.lee@blueskyretail.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-09T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Severe degradation during peak - checkout failures and throughput drop (May 8-9)

Short technical summary (for readout prep) — preliminary RCA and immediate mitigations. Attachments: rca-draft.pdf, timeline.csv

Timeline (high level):
- 2028-05-08 22:36 UTC: sudden increase in long-tail sequence requests (average seq length +80%) from a subset of clients (regex-filtered) aligned with a third-party recommender rollout.
- 22:40 UTC: autoscaler decision boundary hit for your default pooled capacity; continuous batching queue length rose and per-request latency spiked; concurrent requests queueing exposed a regression in our dynamic KV cache eviction under the specific token distribution.
- 22:45-23:20 UTC: error surface increased as memory pressure led to OOM throttling on 2 nodes; retries caused amplification and briefly saturated the host-level RPC layer producing 500s.

Root cause: interplay of sudden longer sequences from external recommender -> queue length increase -> cache eviction churn -> OOM/retry amplification. In short: workload shape change + cache eviction sensitivity in current kernel path.

Immediate mitigations executed (actions completed during triage):
- Applied emergency routing: checkout routes moved to a reserved small-pool with higher memory headroom (manual override) — reduced 500s within ~6 minutes.
- Temporarily enforced sequence-length cap on incoming requests from the identified client group (safeguard).
- Raised autoscaler sensitivity and increased headroom for the weekend flash sale.

Proposed corrective actions (owners & near-term due dates):
- Fix cache eviction policy to be workload-aware (owner: infra-team lead - Karthik Iyer) — ETA: 2028-05-16 (PR + canary).
- Add token-length anomaly detector to routing layer and auto-throttle high-impact noisy clients (owner: platform-safety - Grace O’Connor) — ETA: 2028-05-13 (initial rule set).
- Backup capacity: permanent reserved capacity for checkout route during events (owner: Ben Carter) — ETA: 2028-05-11 (contract + config).

Next steps for readout: I’ll present the timeline and attach the draft RCA (rca-draft.pdf) and the event timeline (timeline.csv). We recommend a short postmortem doc to be finalized by EOD.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: jordan.lee@blueskyretail.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-09T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priority escalation: checkout throughput & 500s - post-incident commitments

Adding commercial/operational commitments for the readout:

- We can provision a reserved small cluster for BlueSky for peak windows on a short lead time (48 hrs) to guarantee headroom; Ben to own contract amendment and quick provisioning.
- Temporary credit: for the hours impacted (we’ll calculate token cost delta) — propose a one-off credit on next invoice pending final numbers.
- Routing SLA: we’ll enable automatic fallback routing policy for checkout endpoints for 14 days while infra fixes land.

I’ll own the procurement/ops side and coordinate with Accounts and Engineering for the short-term reservation.

-Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jordan.lee@blueskyretail.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-09T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Exec readout summary (post-incident)

Jordan / Lisa — thank you for joining the readout. Below is an executive summary for your leadership team and ours; I’ve attached a one-page slide (exec-readout.docx).

Executive summary (2 bullets):
- What happened: a sudden workload-shape change (longer sequence distribution) interacted with a cache eviction regression causing memory pressure and retries that surfaced as increased latency and 500s. The issue has been mitigated via emergency routing and sequence caps.
- Business impact & commitment: error rate peaked at 4.8% for checkout routes for ~45 mins; we reduced errors to <0.3% after routing to reserved pool. Redwood commits to: delivery of a finalized RCA by 2028-05-10 EOD, deployment of cache policy fix CANARY by 2028-05-16, and a reserved capacity plan for the May 14 flash sale.

Action tracker (short):
- Karthik: RCA final + mitigation PR (2028-05-10 EOD)
- Grace: anomaly detector rule set + canary (2028-05-13)
- Ben: reserved pool contract and provisioning (2028-05-11)
- Marissa: weekly check-ins until May 21 and customer-facing PS plan

We’ll circulate the final RCA with timelines and a postmortem readout slide deck tomorrow.

-grace
Head of Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@blueskyretail.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Lisa Park <lisa.park@blueskyretail.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-09T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exec readout summary (post-incident)

Thanks — the readout was helpful and we appreciate the rapid routing mitigation and the clear owners/dates. We accept the proposed reserved pool for the sale window; please get the contract addendum to our accounts team (accounts@blueskyretail.com).

Two asks:
1) Please share the final RCA doc and slide deck by COB 2028-05-10.
2) Weekly status check-ins (15 mins) on Tuesdays at 9:00 PT through May 21 — coordinate calendar invite and attendee list.

Jordan
Director of Engineering, BlueSky Retail
